chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, who said:

We intended to go out, so we came to greet Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said: 'It is as if you are seeking the blessing of Monday.' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And which day is greater in ill-omen than the day of Monday, the day in which we lost our Prophet and the Revelation was raised from us? Do not go out, and go out on the day of Wednesday.'

key_terms.فَقَدْنَا: We lost / We were deprived of

ai.seo_question: Why is Monday considered a day of ill-omen for travel in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the inauspicious nature of Monday to the cessation of Revelation and the departure of the Prophet, a day also significant in Shia tradition for the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him). This advice reflects the broader Shia emphasis on aligning personal actions with cosmic and historical spiritual rhythms, distinguishing between the general 'departure' of the Prophet and the specific grief associated with this day.

en.hubeali: H 14940 – A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazaz who said:

We intended to go out, so we went to greet Abu Abdullahasws. So heasws said: ‘It is as if you all are seeking blessings for Monday’. So we said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said: ‘So which day is greater in evil than the day of Monday, the day in which our Prophetsaww departed, and the Revelation was Raised (stopped) from usasws. Do not go out, and go out on the day of Wednesday’.
en.sarwar: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al-Ja’fary, who has narrated: Abu Al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) having said, ‘The evil, for the traveller in his road, are five things – The cawing crow on his right and spreading its tail; and the howling wolf which howls on the face of the man while sitting on it’s tail and raises its voice and lowers it three times; and the deer which crossing from the right to the left, and the crying owl, and an old woman coming in from the front, and confronting a female (astray) donkey. So the one who feels anything from these for himself, so he should immediately say, ‘I adhere to You (azwj), O Lord (azwj), from the evil of what I find in (front of) myself’. He (a.s.) said; ‘He would be protected from that’.
